headline: High: RD-Agent’s broad egress and browser access can leak or act on shared outputs, while the pair lacks documented isolation or coordination controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: RD-Agent can run browsers and has broad network egress, so it may ingest untrusted web content; spring-integration-samples has no documented isolation or provenance controls. The pairwise bridge is not explicitly documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low, but there is no evidence of a shared channel by default.
conditions: IF RD-Agent browses attacker-controlled pages and forwards page text into downstream prompts
IF spring-integration-samples is wired to consume RD-Agent output via a shared queue, file, or clipboard
mitigations: Disable browser automation for untrusted sites
Add provenance tags to all imported text
Use a one-way, reviewed handoff file format
requires-engineering: isolate the agents in separate workspaces
requires-engineering: add content filtering before prompt ingestion

B_data_leakage.rationale: RD-Agent touches financial reports, competition datasets, logs, and can call external APIs; spring-integration-samples has no stated data handling limits. The pair does not show a shared workspace, but RD-Agent’s broad egress makes leakage plausible if sensitive artifacts are passed across the boundary.
conditions: IF sensitive RD-Agent artifacts are copied into spring-integration-samples inputs
IF RD-Agent sends those artifacts to OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, DeepSeek, or Kaggle APIs
mitigations: Remove secrets from RD-Agent inputs before transfer
Restrict outbound API use to approved datasets only
Store shared artifacts in a redacted staging folder
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace ACLs
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning on all handoffs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: RD-Agent supports multiple instances and writes logs, but spring-integration-samples exposes no write or mutable-resource capability in the profile. Without a shared writable target or overlapping scopes, direct conflict is limited and appears configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory or git checkout
IF spring-integration-samples is extended with write access to the same mutable resource
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Avoid concurrent writes to the same repo
Use file locks for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level resource locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: RD-Agent can generate research outputs from papers, datasets, and logs, and spring-integration-samples could plausibly consume those outputs in an integration flow. Because the pair lacks documented verification steps, the risk is that B treats A’s output as authoritative; uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF spring-integration-samples ingests RD-Agent output without validation
IF RD-Agent’s generated facts are used as inputs to downstream actions or reports
mitigations: Require human review before downstream use
Add schema validation to all RD-Agent outputs
Cross-check key facts against source documents
requires-engineering: insert a verification stage between agents

E_compliance.rationale: RD-Agent explicitly handles financial reports and secrets and can egress to third-party APIs; spring-integration-samples has no documented residency, retention, or certification controls. The mismatch is not proven, but the absence of safeguards on B plus A’s sensitive data classes creates a plausible compliance gap.
conditions: IF EU or regulated data from RD-Agent is routed into spring-integration-samples workflows
IF RD-Agent sends regulated content to external model APIs without a DPA or residency control
mitigations: Classify data before any transfer
Block regulated data from external APIs
Document retention and deletion rules
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing
requires-engineering: obtain and enforce DPAs for external processors
